Elena / Marcus — quick technical note to explain our ops controls for the PoC and what evidence we can attach. Summary first, details below:

- No-training: For PoC traffic we will enable a processing flag ("no_improve": true) at the routing layer. That flag prevents interactions from being recorded into any model-improvement pipelines; it is enforced in the inference runtime and at the ingestion service. We can provide a configuration snapshot and the API request header example we use for the PoC.

- KMS/Residency: We support two options for PoC customers in APAC:
  1) Customer-managed KMS via BYOK (you supply KMS credentials/ARN; data keys are wrapped in your key and never exported outside APAC region). Evidence: key-use audit logs + KMS policy snapshot.
  2) Redwood-managed KMS with APAC key residency and strict access controls (SOC2 controls, restricted admin roles, documented key rotation). Evidence: key access audit snippets + region-bound metadata for storage buckets.

- Subprocessors: attached is the current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory.csv). For the PoC we will gate telemetry exports to only approved subprocessors; any other telemetry is disabled by default.

Deliverables we can provide by Apr 5:
- Config snapshot showing routing flag and example request header (no_improve header)
- KMS policy snippet and key-use audit excerpt (redacted) for the APAC cluster
- Subprocessor CSV with a short attestation line for each listed vendor

If Mendel prefers BYOK, we'll need a quick operational runbook call (30m) to exchange credentials and confirm the wrap/unwarp flow.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
SRE, Inference Operations — Redwood Inference

Elena — looping in formally from the legal side. Glad to hear the PoC is moving forward. A few points and suggested language.

1) No-training commitment (sample clause for a short-term PoC):
"Supplier (Redwood) shall not use Customer PoC content, prompts, or responses to update, finetune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models, model weights, or model training datasets during the PoC period. Supplier shall ensure that no PoC data is routed into any model-improvement pipeline and shall provide Customer evidence of such controls on request."

2) Evidence scope: we propose a narrow evidence packet for contracting efficiency: configuration snapshot (ops), KMS audit excerpts (ops), and subprocessor attestation (legal). We will not provide full raw audit logs in contract; instead we provide redacted excerpts and an attestation statement signed by Redwood Security.

3) DPA addendum & next steps: I attached a redline that inserts the above clause plus an evidence delivery schedule (deliverables due Apr 5). If Mendel accepts, we'll put the DPA addendum in the DocuSign envelope. Please review and let us know if you want BYOK or Redwood-managed KMS for the PoC.

DocuSign link (draft envelope): https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/MH-PoC-2028

Kimberly Park
